rationale: The successor experiment ac5f3d92683e42bcb308c9e9c77465ad-experiment has been executed and retained, so this update records its result for the removed-leader investigation on the new basis: the two progress predicates are reproduced and the added boundary control shows that one explicitly triggered campaign by an eligible voter elects a leader and lets a proposal commit. A Fact entry records the instance including the boundary and the stale-leader detail, and the conclusion is stated together with the scope that the observed stall is about the absence of an internal trigger rather than a permanently unrecoverable cluster.

knowledge.statement: In the retained execution of the successor experiment (freshly elected three-voter cluster {1,2,3}, node 1 leader, its own removal proposed, replicated, committed at index 2 and applied on every node with the type-based loop plus applied-index advance, fault-free in-process delivery), the StepDownOnRemoval false probe kept node 1 as StateLeader and out of the configuration (parsed index 0: leader_in_configuration false, voters_after_removal [2,3]) and, across the fixed 80-round window (index 2), no eligible node took leadership (new_leader_elected false, states_after_window all as before), last_index and committed stayed at 2, the leader's own proposal returned 'raft proposal dropped' while a follower's forwarded proposal was dropped at node 1, both followers' election timers stayed at 1, and nothing was undelivered. The ineligible leader still answered a read, but only with a quorum of the current configuration (index 3: one acknowledgment, read_answers 0; index 4: quorum, read_answers 1). After trigger_setup (index 5), a single MsgHup stepped into follower 2 produced a new leader in node 2 (index 6: new_leader_elected true, new_leader_id 2) and a write proposed on that leader committed (index 6: proposal_committed true, last_index_before_proposal 3), while node 1 still reported StateLeader in states_after_trigger because nothing at a higher term reached it. The StepDownOnRemoval true probe elected a leader inside the same window without any trigger (index 9: new_leader_elected true, node 2 StateLeader).
knowledge.conditions: One executed in-process experiment with the fixed harness bytes of experiment ac5f3d92683e42bcb308c9e9c77465ad-experiment (receipt e3485f3513ad4681b8c484e8e2e659d6, exit 0, changed_target_files [], no parsing errors); fault-free delivery, synthetic round-robin ticking of the real timers, no restart, snapshot, partition, joint configuration or operator-side membership change; the external trigger is one MsgHup message, the same path Node.Campaign and a forced election use. One observed instance under these conditions, not a universal guarantee.

interpretations.rationale: Receipt e3485f3513ad4681b8c484e8e2e659d6 is a completed execution of this investigation's successor experiment on the changed basis (status completed, exit 0, outcome tests_passed, unchanged target files, no parsing errors, 10 parsed events). Comparison 0, unchanged in meaning, declares that with StepDownOnRemoval false the cluster elects a new leader inside the fixed progress window without external help; it is violated again with a complete valid witness at parsed index 2, correlated to its own admission at index 1 (progress_setup: step_down_on_removal false, ticks 80, leader_state StateLeader, leader absent from the configuration, voters [2,3]). The operands are new_leader_elected false, states_after_window {1: StateLeader, 2: StateFollower, 3: StateFollower}, last_index 2 and committed 2 before and after, leader_propose_error 'raft proposal dropped' with the follower's forwarded proposal dropped at node 1, follower election timers 1 and 1, and undelivered_messages 0. Comparison 1, the step-down control, holds at index 9 (new_leader_elected true, node 2 in StateLeader), so the same sequence with Config.StepDownOnRemoval true reaches leadership inside the window by itself. Comparison 2 is the added boundary control and holds at index 6, correlated to trigger_setup at index 5: after one MsgHup was stepped into follower 2, node 2 became leader and a write proposed on it committed with last_index_before_proposal 3, so the stall is ended by an explicit eligible-voter campaign rather than being permanent. The read events reproduce the earlier protective observation (index 3: one acknowledgment from the current voters, read_answers 0; index 4: quorum, read_answers 1), and states_after_trigger shows node 1 still reporting StateLeader because it is no longer contacted by the new configuration, which scopes the dual-leader detail to a stale node that has not yet learned of the higher term. Mechanism unchanged and sourced: switchToConfig keeps the role for a removed leader when step-down is not requested (raft.go:1975-2030), stepLeader drops proposals without a progress entry (raft.go:1290-1295), tickHeartbeat keeps broadcasting heartbeats that reset the eligible voters' timers (raft.go:862-889, 692-707), and an eligible voter only takes over when something explicitly makes it campaign (raft.go:973-993 via MsgHup). Engineering significance: the successor reproduces the finding on a new basis and shows the recovery boundary, so the defect claim is about the absence of any internal trigger while an ineligible leader keeps the role, not about an unrecoverable cluster.
counterevidence: Config.StepDownOnRemoval is a documented knob and the control probe (index 9) reaches leadership without help when it is enabled, so the stalled behaviour can be read as the intended consequence of the default setting.

The boundary control (index 6) shows the stall ends as soon as an eligible voter campaigns explicitly, which is the same MsgHup path an operator or a forced election uses; the finding therefore does not claim an unrecoverable state.
The ineligible leader never misuses its role for reads: it answered only after a quorum of the current configuration acknowledged (indices 3 and 4).

After the trigger node 1 still reports StateLeader because it is not contacted at a higher term, so it can remain a harmless stale leader; this dual-view detail is a boundary of the observation, not evidence of a second defect.
The harness ticks nodes in a fixed round-robin order with prompt delivery, so the window is a normal-opportunity schedule rather than a proof about every schedule.
limitations: One execution on the changed basis with a synthetic tick schedule and fault-free in-process delivery; the observation is bounded to those conditions.
Simple removal of the leader in a three-voter cluster only; joint configurations, learners, demotion and larger or smaller clusters were not exercised.
The external trigger is a single MsgHup message from the harness; how quickly an operator or embedding service would act in a real deployment is outside the captured package.
Whether a membership controller is expected to configure step-down or to intervene is a contract question outside the snapshot, so severity classification remains with human review.
This interpretation covers the successor experiment only; the predecessor interpretation for the original basis remains recorded and was not revised.
interpretations.report_title: 被移除 leader 不下台时的进度停滞：新 basis 复现，且需外部触发才能恢复
interpretations.report_answer: 在 successor 实验（同一移除场景、新增外部触发阶段）中：StepDownOnRemoval=false 时被移除的 node 1 仍为 StateLeader，80 轮窗口内没有新的合格 leader、last_index 与 committed 均停在 2、其自身提案返回 'raft proposal dropped'、被转发的 follower 提案同样被丢弃、两个 follower 的选举计时器停在 1、无未投递消息；读路径仍受保护（1 个确认→0 应答，quorum→1 应答）。随后仅向 follower 2 注入一次 MsgHup，node 2 立即成为 leader 并且在其上提交的写入成功（proposal_committed=true），说明停滞由“缺少内部触发”造成而非集群不可恢复；StepDownOnRemoval=true 的对照在同样窗口内自行选出 leader。该记录同时保留 node 1 因未收到更高 term 消息而仍自称 leader 的细节，作为观察边界。是否构成缺陷需人工结合默认配置与运维契约复核。
